card.name: Ballroom dance
card.era: Roots traced to late 16th century (Arbeau's Orchésographie, 1588); modern competitive form early 20th century
card.tagline: Elegant partnered social and competitive dances, from waltz to quickstep.
card.profile: Ballroom dance is a set of European partner dances enjoyed socially and competitively worldwide. Per Encyclopædia Britannica, it is a type of social dancing originally practiced in Europe and the United States, performed by couples following prescribed steps, historically distinguished from folk dance by its association with elite social classes and invitational dance events. With the rise of DanceSport the term narrowed to the dances recognized by two principal schools - the International School (Standard and Latin) and the American School (Smooth and Rhythm) (Wikipedia).
card.insight: Ballroom dance democratized over the 20th century from an aristocratic pastime into a global social and competitive activity, popularized by figures such as Vernon and Irene Castle, Fred Astaire, and Arthur Murray (Encyclopædia Britannica).
